Bug_Details:
According to the J2EE specification, an EJB should not have any static fields
with write access. However, static read-only fields are allowed. This ensures proper
behavior especially when instances are distributed by the container on several JREs.
Examples:
public class SomeEJB extends EJBObject implements EJBLocalHome {

    private static int CountA;          // poor, field can be edited

    private static final int CountB;    // preferred, read-only access
}
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that this EJB class has a static field that can be edited, which is against the J2EE specification. This can lead to improper behavior when instances are distributed by the container on several JREs.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by creating multiple instances of BuggyEJB and incrementing the CountA field which is not final. This causes the count to be shared between instances, violating the J2EE specification.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results demonstrate that the bug was triggered. The test created two instances of BuggyEJB and incremented the count in each instance. However, the count was not as expected because the static field CountA is not final and can be edited. This violates the J2EE specification and confirms the presence of the described bug in the Java code.
